subject: Nebula Health RFP: commercial clarification - scaling fees, surge credits & billing
messages:
From: Ethan Shaw <eshaw@nebulahealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nebulahealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: commercial clarifications - token floors / surge pricing

Soojin,

Thanks for the initial RFP response. Procurement had a couple of follow-ups on the commercial section where we need specific language/examples to include in the SOW and procurement packet. Short list below — can you confirm by EOD tomorrow?

1) Token classification and per-unit list prices (prompt vs. completion vs. embeddings) and whether embeddings are billed per vector or per 1K vectors.
2) Commit mechanics: monthly vs. annual commits; how discounts scale with volume; how unused committed tokens are handled (rollover, expiration, credits).
3) Surge/burst handling: we need a mechanism for predictable burst capacity for clinical release cycles. Is there a pre-purchased surge pool? How does pricing for surge usage differ from base and overage?
4) Overage rates and smoothing: you mentioned "smoothing credits" in the RFP response. Please provide a sample invoice for the month with a 30% surge and a 10% smoothing credit applied.
5) Billing cap: can we set a hard monthly cap to avoid surprise spend? If yes, what is the scope (per-project, per-account)?
6) Legal/finance: we will need an estimate of committed spend to get internal approvals (USD amount on the sample invoice).

Attached is Nebula appendix C (expected volume profile). We'll share a refined monthly token distribution tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Ethan Shaw
Head of Platform Procurement
Nebula Health

Attachments: Nebula_RFP_Appendix_C.pdf (1 page summary of expected monthly distribution)

From: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Shaw <eshaw@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: commercial clarifications - token floors / surge pricing

Ethan — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; we attached a worked example (RW_Pricing_Example_Nebula.xlsx) that runs the math against the appendix C volumes. If those numbers look sensible we can convert to SOW language.

Summary (high level):
- Token classification & units: prompt tokens billed at $0.0009/token; completion tokens billed at $0.0018/token; embeddings billed at $0.00045/vector. Embeddings are invoiced per vector (we do not bucket by 1K vectors by default, but we can show an alternate view on the invoice).
- Commit mechanics: we offer monthly or annual pre-commit. Annual pre-pay gets an incremental discount ladder (12-month prepay: additional 5% over monthly commit discounts). Unused committed tokens carry as credits that expire at the end of the 12-month term unless otherwise contractually extended.
- Surge/burst model: we offer a "surge pool" option: customer prepurchases surge credits (in token equivalents) at a lower uplift than ad-hoc overage and draws from that pool when usage spikes. If the surge pool is exhausted, overages apply automatically.
- Overage & smoothing credits: base overage is charged at 140% of the list per-token rate. Smoothing credits are applied as a negotiated fractional credit to the invoice line for the month when variance is within the agreed smoothing window (we typically apply up to 10% smoothing credit for a single-month spike once per quarter).
- Billing caps: we support a soft monthly notification cap by default and can enable a hard spend cap at account level with two caveats: (1) if set, calls beyond the cap are throttled (caller receives 429) — not recommended for critical clinical flows, and (2) hard cap requires acceptance of potential availability reduction and is governed in the account-level config.

Next steps: we need the monthly profile from your appendix so we can populate the example invoice. Laura — adding you for the invoice math and discount ladder; Karthik — can you flag any legal language we need for the credit expiry and hard cap behavior?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RW_Pricing_Example_Nebula.xlsx (pricing model, sample invoices)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Ethan Shaw <eshaw@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 14:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: commercial clarifications - pricing worked example and terms

Ethan — pulled the numbers together and attached the populated spreadsheet. Below is a concise, line-by-line example using the volumes from your profile and two commercial configurations so you can compare immediately: hard cap (throttle) vs. standard overage billing.

Assumptions used (monthly):
- Monthly committed baseline: 120M tokens (mixed prompt/completion split 30/70)
- Embeddings: 10K vectors/month
- Base list rates: prompt $0.0009/token, completion $0.0018/token, embedding $0.00045/vector
- Commit discount: 20% off list at the 120M/month tier (applied pro rata across classes)
- Annual prepay additional: 5% (applied after the commit discount)
- Surge pool: pre-purchase 20M tokens at a 25% uplift over list (i.e., surge pool price = list * 1.25 reduced by commit discount if applied at purchase time)
- Overage: 140% of list for any ad-hoc usage beyond commit + surge pool
- Smoothing credit: up to 10% credit on the invoice line for single-month surges (once per quarter) if monthly variance < 35% and customer enrolls in smoothing program

Configuration A — Standard (no hard cap):
- Committed billed at discounted rates: net per-token cost (post commit & annual prepay) approx. prompt $0.000576, completion $0.001152
- Usage spike: month shows 30% over baseline (36M extra tokens). Draws first from surge pool (20M at surge price) then hits overage for remaining 16M at 140% of list.
- Smoothing credit applicable: we applied a 10% smoothing credit to the overage portion (per program rules) which reduces the overage effective rate in the example.
- Resulting sample invoice total (USD): $41,200 (breakdown in attached sheet).

Configuration B — Hard cap (throttle):
- Hard spend cap set to the same nominal monthly spend as Configuration A's committed+surge budget.
- Excess calls past cap are throttled and return 429; no overage line appears on the invoice.
- Resulting availability during the surge window is reduced; sample invoice total (USD): $38,900 (lower because no overage invoices but potential impact on availability).

Surge pooling scoping:
- Surge pools can be scoped per project (we implement at the project-level namespace). If you want cross-project pooling that's also possible but needs to be explicit in the SOW.
- Surge credits: standard life is 12 months from purchase. Expiry can be extended contractually (we offer a 6- or 12-month extension at signing).

Billing metadata & SOC2:
- We provide line-item metadata (project id, model id, route id, timestamp) on all invoices and can redact PII before sending to procurement if required by your security team. No impact to the commercial math.

Next steps: attached populated RW_Pricing_Example_Nebula.xlsx with line-by-line math, an example invoice PDF, and a redline of the relevant SOW clauses to capture surge pool scoping and credit expiry. If these look good, we can convert to a commercial exhibit and start the signature path.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Principal Commercial Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: RW_Pricing_Example_Nebula.xlsx; Redwood_Master_SA_v3_for_NEBULA.pdf
